title: Brain in a Vat
summary: What if your brain had been removed from your body, kept alive in a vat of nutrients, and wired to a computer that feeds it a perfect simulation of the world? Everything would feel exactly as it does now. So how could you ever know it isn't happening? The idea descends from René Descartes' evil demon (1641), who might deceive us about everything. Hilary Putnam gave it its modern form in 1981, then answered it: if we were brains in vats, our words would not refer to real brains and vats at all, so we could not even truly think that we were. The objections to his reply keep the debate alive.
